page: Amazon Web Services r5.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, offering 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled. The processor includes 35 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 384 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network performance is defined with a 12 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes zero GPUs and no local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded capabilities balanced against lower single-thread throughput. Single-core tests such as Geekbench and stress-ng place the instance in the bottom 25% of measured systems, accompanied by single-threaded gzip compression at 23.35 GB/sec. When parallelized across all 48 vCPUs, multi-threaded metrics scale into median ranges. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 34676.69, a multi-core Geekbench score of 10528.0, and 37.65 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 110.33 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 49.35 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5.12xlarge allocates budget heavily toward high-capacity DDR4 memory allocation rather than raw per-thread computing power or integrated disk IOPS. The trade-off involves subdued single-core execution speed and the need to provision separate network-attached storage. Consequently, the instance is targeted at memory-intensive enterprise tasks, including large in-memory caching tiers like Redis or Memcached, relational databases with extensive working sets, distributed analytics, and batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r5.12xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro hypervisor platform. Powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor, it delivers 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs alongside 384 GB of DDR4 system memory, reflecting an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance features no local storage and lacks GPU accelerators, relying on a 12 Gbps baseline network link for connectivity and network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread execution speeds contrasting with stable multi-threaded efficiency, evidenced by solid multi-core processing, 110.33 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, and 37.65 million Redis operations per second. Given its resource distribution, the instance provides qualitative resource density for memory-bound applications without overhead from local disks. It is appropriately deployed for in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, distributed data processing, and enterprise application deployments requiring substantial operational memory.
